newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia, Germany pledge to deepen cultural ties.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia, Germany pledge to deepen cultural ties.

text.p: Malaysia and Germany agreed on Wednesday to expand ties through more cultural and education exchange programmes, deepening relations beyond trade and economic cooperation.

Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi, briefing reporters after talks with German Vice Chancellor and Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel, said Germany had proposed that the two countries sign a cultural agreement.
"We must now think of an expanded relationship that is not confined to trade but also includes education and science and technology cooperation," Badawi said.
Abdullah said he discussed Burma, Bosnia and the Spratlys, a disputed island chain in the South China Sea, with Kinkel, the first German foreign minister to visit Malaysia in 16 years.

Abdullah said Kinkel reacted positively to a proposal that Malaysia and Germany form a partnership to help in the former Yugoslav republic's reconstruction. Moslem Malaysia has been a staunch supporter of the Bosnian government.
Kinkel arrived on Wednesday afternoon on an abbreviated trip, accompanied by a 98-member delegation consisting mostly of businessmen.

Kinkel was originally scheduled to arrive on Tuesday for a two-day visit, but that was shortened so he could attend the signing of a German-Czech post-World War Two reconciliation agreement in Prague.
Kinkel is scheduled to leave on Thursday morning for India.
